title: Research checklist
use_cases: Use when preparing a content draft to ensure factual accuracy and source depth
Configure when managing sensitive themes or legal concerns regarding direct quotations
Implement when covering active fan debates to preemptively address objections
Use when verifying technical details like publication dates and translation choices
content:
Before you draft, confirm that you have the source text, at least one secondary analysis, and a clear audience goal. Define your angle in one sentence, then list the 3–5 claims your piece will make. Note any sensitive themes, disputed interpretations, or legal concerns, especially if your content uses direct quotation, screenshots, or clips. If you are covering a living franchise or a work with active fan debate, keep a log of likely objections and how you will address them.

A good checklist should also include verification steps. For example: double-check character names, publication dates, edition differences, and translation choices. If you reference market behavior or cultural relevance, look for current data or recent coverage rather than relying on memory. This is similar to how smart creators use AI-powered market research to test whether a new idea has enough audience demand to justify production. Research first, opinion second.
